column2: In Claude Code, even just dismissing the feedback may be considered "feedback". I wrote about it here: https://keydiscussions.com/2025/09/29/dont-even-dismiss-the-... The most common feedback on these posts is always "what did you expect?" ....... Man, the reason I signed up for one service over the other in the first place is often because of the promises these companies make on the front end, about what they do or don't do with my data. I agree that the bar is low in the industry but it doesn't mean we shouldn't expect more. Anthropic made very explicit, strong promises in this area , and so of course it disappoints me when I feel like the company I'm paying hundreds of dollars per month to is trying to sneak a peak. I literally think differently and self-censor when I think my work is being surveilled or stolen, which makes me less productive.

In a company as big as Anthropic, moving at current pace, the person/team writing this article and the team(s) collecting data would be way distant. It should be more than obvious that the data is being collected in not just one place but many (different teams are looking for different gems in that data). What part is used for training, how and when would be spread across the company way too wide for anyone to confirm with certainity.

  On the IP side, About 6 months ago I used Claude to help me draft a patent application for something which I believed was novel, I verified in the USPTO as well. Then out of being busy I dropped that idea. Couple weeks ago I picked up the work again, verified with Claude for the problem statement to see if there is any existing solution. It suggested my own solution back to me which was surprising since I only use in browser and delete the history explicitly. I asked it for references or resources and it could not find any. That helped me to understand the boundaries bit better.
There are companies with far more people than Anthropic that still stay coordinated. This is no excuse. Especially with customer data.

I have noticed this as well, when it can't help me and I thought it might be a difference in models, or using the same account somehow (tried a different one).

The Claude Code data usage policy covers this - none of the options change your data retention or training opt-in: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage#session-quality-s...

"When you see the “How is Claude doing this session?” prompt in Claude Code, responding to this survey, including selecting “Dismiss”, records only your rating. We do not collect or store any conversation transcripts, inputs, outputs, or other session data as part of the rating prompt itself. Unlike thumbs up/down feedback or /feedback reports, this session quality survey is a simple product satisfaction metric."

Is it because you view frontier AI labs as beneficial entities that truly care about everyone's well-being, and will do what it takes to ensure, post-replacement, that we are 'taken care of', broadly speaking? Or are you more like "I'm ready to be replaced, and if that results in my death, I was over this reality in the first place, so it just speeds up what I've been hankering for anyway."

If I'm replaced, it will mean that humanity as a whole has taken a step forward that's normally associated with digging up monoliths. If nothing else, it'll mean that I'll get to do something more interesting.

I'm one of those "code to live" types, as opposed to someone who "lives to code." More specifically, I usually write code in the course of building something that uses it. That's true 99% of the time, anyway. Why would I complain about a technology that helps me (and my customers and employers) move closer to the actual goal?

As for resulting in my death, AI is not going to be what kills me. Not unless humans misuse it. Which, of course, we will, because that's what we do... but (shrug) if it's misused in a way that kills me, at least it'll be a more interesting death. More likely, it will extend my life by accelerating medical progress the way it's starting to accelerate progress in math.

In any case, I don't see the current crop of frontier labs being especially important in the grand scheme of things. Unless they have something up their sleeves besides serving LLM tokens, they are most likely the pets.com and Webvan of our day, not the Amazon and Apple. They are valuable partners, certainly, but I can get by without them.
